A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCOPE research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The complete material supports comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix B report original Gridworld and five MuJoCo simulation experiments comparing estimation error, variance, and execution cost.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally tabulates numerical summaries of the Gridworld results in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the backward behavior-policy optimization, extended-reward recursion, and offline learning procedure are unchanged. The correction to the global constraint in Equation (12) aligns it with the target-relative constraint already used by the algorithm; it does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,000- and 27,000-state Gridworlds and the same five MuJoCo tasks: Ant, Hopper, InvertedDoublePendulum, InvertedPendulum, and Walker. The additional Gridworld tables introduce no new task or environment coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding Gridworld and MuJoCo comparisons retain on-policy Monte Carlo, robust on-policy sampling (ROS), and offline data informed estimation (ODI). Added citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the reported source of the 1,000 offline episodes from a set of random policies to 30 policies spanning random initialization through well-trained performance. This is a limited reported data-generation revision; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. The principal evaluation budgets and settings are retained.

E4.justification: No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is introduced. The additional Gridworld tables summarize existing benchmark comparisons, and the appendix plot with logarithmic axes is retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 target policies with 30 independent runs each, totaling 900 runs, and use standard-error shading. The added tables and caption wording repeat this reporting practice without introducing new run counts, uncertainty procedures, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Tables 3–4 provide Gridworld numerical summaries, including SCOPE relative variances of 0.547/0.575 and accuracy-matched costs of 472/487. Existing plots and MuJoCo table values are unchanged. The new cost entries are not reconciled with the retained Section 7 Gridworld example reporting SCOPE cost 425 and ODI cost 880.

T1.justification: Equation (12) changes the global constraint from J^c(mu) <= (1 + epsilon) to J^c(mu) <= (1 + epsilon)J^c(pi), correcting its inconsistency with the existing target-relative guarantee. Theorems 1 and 3 explicitly state epsilon >= 0, already assumed in the surrounding text. Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about constrained variance minimization, unbiased evaluation, variance reduction, and execution safety. Adding 'Off-Policy' to the title clarifies the existing scope rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: The discussion after Theorem 3 newly emphasizes that the step-wise safety constraint is stricter than the global constraint. Appendix B.2 also explains the safety rationale for action-based control costs through abrupt robot-state changes. The limitation concerning insufficient offline data and the recommended on-policy fallback remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies the MuJoCo control cost as the action's L2 norm, identifies 30 offline-data-generating policies, and gives their approximate Hopper performance range of 18–2800. These improve implementation documentation; the previously reported FQE procedure, network size, optimizer settings, and action discretization are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds safe-RL survey citations, three Liu et al. (2024) papers, and Brockman et al. (2016), while distinguishing safe exploration from safe optimization in Section 2. This modestly broadens context without substantially changing the central positioning against variance-reduction methods that omit safety constraints.

P1.justification: The title and author text are updated, several introduction, related-work, background, and experimental-detail paragraphs are edited, and acknowledgements become unnumbered. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Appendix B gains two small Gridworld tables; the existing MuJoCo Tables 3–4 become Tables 5–6. Figure 5 moves from page 21 to page 22, and conference headers, spacing, and captions change. Existing plots and robot images are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (12) improves consistency with the existing safety guarantee, while the added cost-function and data-generation details improve transparency and reproducibility. The Gridworld tables make existing evidence more explicit. These are limited gains: the core method and evidence remain stable, and Table 4's costs of 472/487 are not reconciled with Section 7's retained 425-cost example.
